dek: Two Olympic National Park waterfalls: Marymere Falls (1.8 miles round trip) and Sol Duc Falls (1.1 miles one way). See the best season, fees and trail notes.
overview: Olympic National Park covers nearly a million acres of glacier-capped mountains, temperate rain forest and more than 70 miles of wild coastline.

We cover two waterfalls, in different valleys. Marymere Falls, near Lake Crescent, is 0.9 mile one way (1.8 miles round trip) and has the most visitor reviews. The park's notes say it flows year-round and is strongest from fall through spring. Sol Duc Falls is 1.1 miles one way, on the Sol Duc River southeast of Sol Duc Hot Springs.
fallsIntro: Marymere Falls is listed as a round trip because the source gives both numbers. Sol Duc Falls is listed one way.
plan: Marymere Falls is the easy one: 1.8 miles round trip, with stairs up to the upper and lower viewpoints, and it flows year-round. Sol Duc Falls is a separate 1.1-mile one-way walk in a different drainage, so plan one valley per day rather than combining them.
flow: The nearest gauge with a complete record is the Elwha River at McDonald Bridge near Port Angeles (USGS 12045500), about 9.5 miles from Marymere Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in January at about 2,850 cubic feet per second and was lowest in September at about 439.
Marymere's own note, strongest from fall through spring, is the better timing guide for that waterfall. The gauge describes a different river.
feesLead: A standard seven-day vehicle pass covers the entrance. We found no timed-entry rule on the park's fee page.
access: The park's fee page sends wilderness camping, filming and lodging to separate permit pages. Day hikes to these two waterfalls are covered by the entrance pass. Both falls are filed under Port Angeles, but Sol Duc Hot Springs is the better landmark for Sol Duc Falls.
safety: Marymere Falls is rated easy, with stairs at the viewpoints, and Sol Duc Falls is a short walk with an easy hiking rating (SAC T1). We have no waterfall-specific warnings on file. The park does say weather can differ by 10 to 20 degrees between the coast and the high country, so pack for the valley you're visiting.
